blocks.prompt: 4 (i) Use synthetic division to show that \(x\) is the zero of the polynomial and use the result to factorize the polynomial completely: \(x^{3} - 7x + 6\), \(x = 2\).
blocks.explanation:
A zero of a polynomial is a value of \(x\) that makes it 0. If synthetic division by \(x - a\) leaves remainder 0, then \(a\) is a zero and \(x - a\) is a factor.
We must show the given value is a zero, then factorize completely.
Plan: synthetic division, read the quotient, factorize the quadratic quotient, write all factors.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = x^{3} - 7x + 6\), \(x = 2\).
To find: show this is a zero; factorize \(f(x)\) completely.
Method: Synthetic division by \(x - a\). Remainder 0 means \(a\) is a zero and \(x - a\) is a factor (factor theorem); the bottom row gives the quotient, which we factorize further.

Synthetic division of \(x^{3} - 7x + 6\) by \(x - 2\) (\(a = 2\))
\[\begin{array}{r|rrrr} 2 & 1 & 0 & -7 & 6 \\  &  & 2 & 4 & -6 \\ \hline & 1 & 2 & -3 & \boxed{0} \end{array}\]
\[1 \times 2 = 2,\ 0 + 2 = 2\]
\[2 \times 2 = 4,\ -7 + 4 = -3\]
\[-3 \times 2 = -6,\ 6 + (-6) = 0\]
Why: Bring down the first coefficient; then multiply by \(2\) and add, column by column. There is no \(x^{2}\) term, so 0 is written in its place.

Read the result
\[\text{Remainder} = 0\]
So \(x = 2\) is a zero and \(x - 2\) is a factor.
\[\text{Quotient} = x^{2} + 2x - 3\]
Why: The boxed last number is the remainder. The other bottom numbers are the coefficients of the quotient, one degree lower.

Write \(f(x)\) with the factors found
\[f(x) = (x - 2)(x^{2} + 2x - 3)\]
Why: Dividend = Divisor × Quotient, because the remainder is 0.

Factorize the quadratic quotient
\[x^{2} + 2x - 3\]
\[= x^{2} + 3x - x - 3\]
\[= x(x + 3) - 1(x + 3)\]
\[= (x + 3)(x - 1)\]
Why: Split the middle term: we need two numbers with product \(-3\) and sum \(2\); they are \(3\) and \(-1\). Then take common factors in pairs.

Write the complete factorization
\[x^{3} - 7x + 6\]
\[= (x - 2)(x - 1)(x + 3)\]
Why: Every factor is now linear (degree 1), so nothing more can be factorized.

Check: put \(x = 0\) in both forms
\[f(0) = 6\]
\[(-2)(-1)(3) = 6 \;\checkmark\]
Why: The polynomial and its factorized form must give the same value for any \(x\).

blocks.prompt: 4 (ii) Use synthetic division to show that \(x\) is the zero of the polynomial and use the result to factorize the polynomial completely: \(x^{3} - 28x - 48\), \(x = -4\).
blocks.explanation:
A zero of a polynomial is a value of \(x\) that makes it 0. If synthetic division by \(x - a\) leaves remainder 0, then \(a\) is a zero and \(x - a\) is a factor.
We must show the given value is a zero, then factorize completely.
Plan: synthetic division, read the quotient, factorize the quadratic quotient, write all factors.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = x^{3} - 28x - 48\), \(x = -4\).
To find: show this is a zero; factorize \(f(x)\) completely.
Method: Synthetic division by \(x - a\). Remainder 0 means \(a\) is a zero and \(x - a\) is a factor (factor theorem); the bottom row gives the quotient, which we factorize further.

Synthetic division of \(x^{3} - 28x - 48\) by \(x + 4\) (\(a = -4\))
\[\begin{array}{r|rrrr} -4 & 1 & 0 & -28 & -48 \\  &  & -4 & 16 & 48 \\ \hline & 1 & -4 & -12 & \boxed{0} \end{array}\]
\[1 \times (-4) = -4,\ 0 + (-4) = -4\]
\[-4 \times (-4) = 16,\ -28 + 16 = -12\]
\[-12 \times (-4) = 48,\ -48 + 48 = 0\]
Why: Bring down the first coefficient; then multiply by \(-4\) and add, column by column. There is no \(x^{2}\) term, so 0 is written in its place.

Read the result
\[\text{Remainder} = 0\]
So \(x = -4\) is a zero and \(x + 4\) is a factor.
\[\text{Quotient} = x^{2} - 4x - 12\]
Why: The boxed last number is the remainder. The other bottom numbers are the coefficients of the quotient, one degree lower.

Write \(f(x)\) with the factors found
\[f(x) = (x + 4)(x^{2} - 4x - 12)\]
Why: Dividend = Divisor × Quotient, because the remainder is 0.

Factorize the quadratic quotient
\[x^{2} - 4x - 12\]
\[= x^{2} - 6x + 2x - 12\]
\[= x(x - 6) + 2(x - 6)\]
\[= (x - 6)(x + 2)\]
Why: Split the middle term: we need two numbers with product \(-12\) and sum \(-4\); they are \(-6\) and \(2\). Then take common factors in pairs.

Write the complete factorization
\[x^{3} - 28x - 48\]
\[= (x + 4)(x - 6)(x + 2)\]
Why: Every factor is now linear (degree 1), so nothing more can be factorized.

Check: put \(x = 0\) in both forms
\[f(0) = -48\]
\[(4)(-6)(2) = -48 \;\checkmark\]
Why: The polynomial and its factorized form must give the same value for any \(x\).

blocks.prompt: 4 (iii) Use synthetic division to show that \(x\) is the zero of the polynomial and use the result to factorize the polynomial completely: \(2x^{4} + 7x^{3} - 4x^{2} - 27x - 18\), \(x = 2, x = -3\).
blocks.explanation:
A zero of a polynomial is a value of \(x\) that makes it 0. If synthetic division by \(x - a\) leaves remainder 0, then \(a\) is a zero and \(x - a\) is a factor.
We must show the given values are zeros, then factorize completely.
Plan: synthetic division, read the quotient, factorize the quadratic quotient, write all factors.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = 2x^{4} + 7x^{3} - 4x^{2} - 27x - 18\), \(x = 2, x = -3\).
To find: show these are zeros; factorize \(f(x)\) completely.
Method: Synthetic division by \(x - a\). Remainder 0 means \(a\) is a zero and \(x - a\) is a factor (factor theorem); the bottom row gives the quotient, which we factorize further.

Synthetic division of \(2x^{4} + 7x^{3} - 4x^{2} - 27x - 18\) by \(x - 2\) (\(a = 2\))
\[\begin{array}{r|rrrrr} 2 & 2 & 7 & -4 & -27 & -18 \\  &  & 4 & 22 & 36 & 18 \\ \hline & 2 & 11 & 18 & 9 & \boxed{0} \end{array}\]
\[2 \times 2 = 4,\ 7 + 4 = 11\]
\[11 \times 2 = 22,\ -4 + 22 = 18\]
\[18 \times 2 = 36,\ -27 + 36 = 9\]
\[9 \times 2 = 18,\ -18 + 18 = 0\]
Why: Bring down the first coefficient; then multiply by \(2\) and add, column by column.

Read the result
\[\text{Remainder} = 0\]
So \(x = 2\) is a zero and \(x - 2\) is a factor.
\[\text{Quotient} = 2x^{3} + 11x^{2} + 18x + 9\]
Why: The boxed last number is the remainder. The other bottom numbers are the coefficients of the quotient, one degree lower.

Synthetic division of the quotient \(2x^{3} + 11x^{2} + 18x + 9\) by \(x + 3\) (\(a = -3\))
\[\begin{array}{r|rrrr} -3 & 2 & 11 & 18 & 9 \\  &  & -6 & -15 & -9 \\ \hline & 2 & 5 & 3 & \boxed{0} \end{array}\]
\[2 \times (-3) = -6,\ 11 + (-6) = 5\]
\[5 \times (-3) = -15,\ 18 + (-15) = 3\]
\[3 \times (-3) = -9,\ 9 + (-9) = 0\]
Why: Bring down the first coefficient; then multiply by \(-3\) and add, column by column.

Read the result
\[\text{Remainder} = 0\]
So \(x = -3\) is a zero and \(x + 3\) is a factor.
\[\text{Quotient} = 2x^{2} + 5x + 3\]
Why: The boxed last number is the remainder. The other bottom numbers are the coefficients of the quotient, one degree lower.

Write \(f(x)\) with the factors found
\[f(x) = (x - 2)(x + 3)(2x^{2} + 5x + 3)\]
Why: Dividend = Divisor × Quotient, because the remainder is 0.

Factorize the quadratic quotient
\[2x^{2} + 5x + 3\]
\[= 2x^{2} + 2x + 3x + 3\]
\[= 2x(x + 1) + 3(x + 1)\]
\[= (x + 1)(2x + 3)\]
Why: Split the middle term: we need two numbers with product \(6\) and sum \(5\); they are \(2\) and \(3\). Then take common factors in pairs.

Write the complete factorization
\[2x^{4} + 7x^{3} - 4x^{2} - 27x - 18\]
\[= (x - 2)(x + 3)(x + 1)(2x + 3)\]
Why: Every factor is now linear (degree 1), so nothing more can be factorized.

Check: put \(x = 0\) in both forms
\[f(0) = -18\]
\[(-2)(3)(1)(3) = -18 \;\checkmark\]
Why: The polynomial and its factorized form must give the same value for any \(x\).
